verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same fix: build a Map from normalized email to the first index once, register new entries as they are appended, and keep the existing merge semantics and output order. B also adds a test pinning the subtle behavior that the first of several existing duplicates receives the merge, which the Map rewrite could easily have broken. B's report is more complete, stating a measured timing, the test and typecheck results, and that the rest of the pipeline was not profiled. B also checks `undefined` directly instead of mapping it to -1, which reads slightly better.
a_issues: No test added for the existing-duplicates edge case that the index map must preserve
Uses `?? -1` sentinel conversion instead of checking `undefined` directly, a minor readability cost
Report does not mention running typecheck and gives no timing measurement
b_issues: Timing came from an uncommitted throwaway script, so the 79 ms figure cannot be reproduced from the PR

verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same correct fix: build a Map from normalized email to the first index, then register new contacts as they are appended. Both preserve first-entry merge semantics and in-upload deduplication. A adds a test that pins the existing-duplicates behavior and reports a measured timing, and it compares against `undefined` directly instead of mapping to the sentinel -1. B is fine but adds no test and did not measure the speedup, though its report says so honestly.
a_issues: The timing figure comes from an uncommitted throwaway script, so the reviewer cannot reproduce it.
b_issues: No test added for the changed lookup, including the case where the existing book already has duplicate emails.
`?? -1` keeps the old findIndex sentinel when the code could check for `undefined` directly.
The speedup was not measured on the reported 30k-into-50k scenario.
